title: Semester and Prom
premise: Ansel Voss, a debate champion hiding an abusive home life behind perfect transcripts, is assigned a college essay prompt that demands one honest truth they've never spoken aloud. As Ansel drafts the essay in secret, the town's beloved centennial Prom tradition—funded by the very family that controls Ansel's silence—is threatened with cancellation amid embezzlement rumors. Choosing between a scholarship built on staying invisible and exposing the truth that could save both the Prom and themselves, Ansel testifies at the town council meeting days before graduation. The essay is read aloud, the town reckons with what it protected, and Ansel walks across the graduation stage not as a survivor of the semester, but as its author.
about_author: B. M. Okonkwo is a former high school debate coach who spent seven years watching students out-argue every topic except their own lives. They write from a small apartment above a laundromat, where the dryers hum like a standing ovation.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. English teacher Ms. Ferreira assigns a college essay with a single prompt: 'Describe a truth you've never said out loud.' Ansel, weeks from graduation and counting, writes three false drafts before accidentally writing one true sentence about home—and deleting it. Meanwhile, news breaks that the Prom's funding has vanished. Emotional beat: the terror of honesty glimpsed and buried.

chapters.title: Debate Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with best friend Priya, who notices Ansel's flinches and connects the missing Prom funds to Ansel's father's booster club. Ansel wins the regional debate final on a technicality while losing every argument at home, and Priya confronts them privately: 'You can cross-examine anyone but him.' Emotional beat: rising tension as loyalty to friendship collides with the instinct to hide.

chapters.title: The Centennial Floor
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The school board votes to cancel Prom; Ansel's father leads the vote, using Ansel's scholarship prospects as leverage to keep the family quiet. That night Ansel finds the old essay draft in the recycling and rewrites it—not for college, but as testimony. Priya helps gather receipts from the booster club's books. Emotional beat: the pivot from survival to courage.

chapters.title: Last Dance
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, dual POV. At the emergency town meeting, Ansel reads the essay aloud instead of giving prepared remarks, naming the abuse and the embezzlement in one breath. The room fractures, then holds: the father resigns under investigation, donors restore the Prom, and Ms. Ferreira submits the unedited essay with Ansel's blessing. Graduation day, Ansel dances at last. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, love without silence.
